title: 2024 AMC 10A Problem 19
statement: The first three terms of a geometric sequence are the integers \(a,\) \(720,\) and \(b,\) where \(a \lt 720 \lt b.\) What is the sum of the digits of the least possible value of \(b?\)

solutions.text: Since \(720^2 = ab,\) the common ratio \(r = \tfrac{720}{a} = \tfrac{b}{720}\) is rational. Write \(r = \tfrac{p}{q}\) in lowest terms with \(p \gt q.\) Then \(a = \tfrac{720q}{p}\) and \(b = \tfrac{720p}{q}\) are integers, which forces \(720\) to be divisible by \(p\) and by \(q.\) To make \(b\) smallest, we want the smallest ratio \(\tfrac{p}{q} \gt 1\) with \(720\) divisible by both \(p\) and \(q,\) which is \(\tfrac{16}{15}.\) That gives \(b = 720 \cdot \tfrac{16}{15} = 768\) (and \(a = 675\)). The digit sum is \(7 + 6 + 8 = 21.\) Thus, E is the correct answer.
hints: \(720^2 = ab,\) so the common ratio is rational; write it as \(\tfrac{p}{q}\) in lowest terms with \(p \gt q\)
Both \(p\) and \(q\) must divide \(720;\) minimize \(b = 720 \cdot \tfrac{p}{q}\) using the smallest ratio \(\tfrac{p}{q} \gt 1\)
